L202@P5: COMMENTS
L203@P5: 1. Author’s statement
L204@P5: According to the author:
L205@P5: As the Attorney General pointed out in a recent settlement with a predatory
L206@P5: landlord, ‘For many renters, especially those from lower income backgrounds,
L207@P5: affording a security deposit entails a great deal of sacrifice.’ By creating a burden
L208@P5: of evidence on the part of the landlord we are giving tenants, especially our most
L209@P5: vulnerable, another tool in the toolbox to protect themselves against egregious
L210@P5: claims of their hard earned money.
L211@P5: 2. The state of renting in California
L212@P5: Almost 17 million Californians rent their apartments or homes, accounting for about 44
L213@P5: percent of all individuals in the state.1 Yet at the same time, California is experiencing
L214@P5: record high prices for homes and rent. In the past decade, median rents in the state have
L215@P5: increased dramatically. In 2022, the median gross rent in the state was $1,870, which
L216@P5: represented about an eight percent increase per year from the median gross rent in
L217@P5: 2019.
L218@P5: 2 As a result for these high rents, significant numbers of California renters pay a
L219@P5: disproportionate amount of their income toward rent and struggle to make ends meet.

L416@P10: 6. AB would be enforced through the courts
L417@P10: If a landlord violates the provisions of Civil Code Section 1950.5, including the
L418@P10: provisions amended or created by this bill, the tenant may pursue a claim against the
L419@P10: landlord through small claims court or through a civil cause of action in court. (Civ.
L420@P10: Code §§ 1950.5(l), (n).) A tenant may obtain statutory damages up to twice the amount
L421@P10: of the security deposit, as well as actual damages, for a bad faith violation of AB 2801’s
L422@P10: provisions. (Civ. Code § 1950.5(l).) However, if a landlord violates the provisions of
L423@P10: Civil Code Section 1950.5 in good faith, a tenant may still pursue an action against the
L424@P10: landlord, but the landlord may offset their damages by any amounts which they could
L425@P10: have properly deducted from the tenant’s deposit originally.9

L429@P11: 7. Arguments in support
L430@P11: According to the Student Homes Coalition, which is a co-sponsor of AB 2801:
L431@P11: The members of the Student HOMES Coalitions believe that every student has
L432@P11: the right to accessible and affordable housing. With the majority of California’s
L433@P11: higher education institutions failing to guarantee undergraduate housing, the
L434@P11: majority of students will have to rent while in college. Faced with limited options
L435@P11: due to lack of available housing near college campuses, students often have to
L436@P11: enter into any available lease. Landlords take advantage of the challenges facing
L437@P11: student renters by refusing to return security deposits or manipulating the
L438@P11: application process to shut out student renters all together. As first-time tenants
L439@P11: often lack resources to contest unfair leasing practices, student renters are
L440@P11: unlikely to get relief through the small claims court process.
L441@P11: AB2801 will address the concerns of student renters while also preserving the
L442@P11: landlord's right to repair any damages caused by the tenant with the security
L443@P11: deposit. Existing law limits the landlord’s claim of a security deposit to only
L444@P11: those amounts as are reasonably necessary for the repair of damages to the
L445@P11: premises, exclusive of ordinary wear and tear, to return the unit to the same level
L446@P11: of cleanliness it was in at the inception of the tenancy. Under the current system,
L447@P11: however, landlords are able to overcharge tenants to subsidize upgrades to the
L448@P11: unit after the termination of the tenancy. Bad-faith retentions like this reduce the
L449@P11: accessibility of housing, as many renters depend on the return of their security
L450@P11: deposit to cover the costs associated with moving to another unit.
L451@P11: By requiring any deductions from the security deposit to be justified with photo
L452@P11: evidence and preventing landlords from making additional claims on a deposit
L453@P11: after a valid initial inspection is conducted, AB 2801 will help protect the security
L454@P11: deposits of tenants and close existing loopholes that allow landlords to violate
L455@P11: the intention of the law.
L456@P11: 8. Arguments in opposition
L457@P11: According to the California Association of Realtors, which is opposed to AB 2801:
L458@P11: AB 2801, among other things, establishes that claims against the tenant or the
L459@P11: security deposit for work performed by a contractor, the housing provider, or the
L460@P11: housing provider’s employee must be limited to a “reasonable” amount
L461@P11: necessary to restore the premises back to the condition it was in at the inception
L462@P11: of the tenancy. It isn’t clear what “reasonable” means in this context, and C.A.R.
L463@P11: is concerned that this lack of clarity could lead to confusion in the marketplace
L464@P11-12: and, in turn, increased litigation.AB 2801 (Friedman)
